Subject: Re: POC - next steps (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

Hi Jared — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through Acme's evaluation criteria. Per our discussion, I summarized the proposed success criteria, recommended evaluation plan, and the environment options for the POC below. See the attached doc for the formal success-criteria template.

Summary / success criteria (draft)
- Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for typical user flows (search + chat)
- Cost: target unit cost goal of <= $0.002/token for bulk batch workloads
- Quality: generation accuracy and hallucination rate within 5% of current baseline on the shared eval set
- Reliability: sustained throughput of 200 reqs/min with graceful degradation

Evaluation plan / timeline (suggested)
- Week 0 (this week): environment kick-off, access & network prep
- Week 1: ingest sample dataset & run smoke tests (latency/cost baseline)
- Week 2: run 48-72h load tests and record metrics; run model A/B for quality checks
- Week 3: finalize results and debrief

Environment options (tradeoffs)
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest setup) — Pros: quick onboarding, no infra for you to manage, streaming and function-calling available. Cons: limited network isolation (public), approximate data residency.
2) Dedicated Sandbox (reserved pool for Acme) — Pros: predictable throughput, isolation at instance level, can be configured with commit for capacity. Cons: longer lead time to reserve GPUs, slightly higher setup time.
3) Private VPC Trial (customer VPC peering or on-prem connector) — Pros: full network isolation, KMS integration, audit logs. Cons: longest setup (cloud networking + security review), we typically run a short checklist/conn day to validate.

Ownership / next steps
- Action for Acme: confirm which environment you want to trial (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC) and provide list of sample dataset endpoints + target eval flows.
- Action for Redwood: once environment chosen we'll share detailed runbook, ephemeral credentials for the trial, and schedule a 1-hour kickoff with engineering.

Proposed kickoff slots:
- Tue Mar 17, 10:00 - 11:00 PT
- Wed Mar 18, 14:00 - 15:00 PT

If you want, Alex can run through the infra checklist during the kickoff to speed the VPC/dedicated setup.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Jared — great, locking Tue Mar 17, 10:00 PT for kickoff. Quick answers on lead times & pre-reqs:

Lead times (typical)
- Hosted trial: immediate — we can provision API keys and a tenant for non-PII traffic within 24 hours.
- Dedicated sandbox: 5-7 business days to allocate a reserved pool and configure capacity for the trial.
- VPC trial: 2-3 weeks typically (networking, peering, and security review).

Pre-reqs for kickoff (hosted path)
- Confirm sample dataset location (S3 or GCS) and a contact for ingestion (SRE + Data Eng).
- Confirm list of evaluation flows and any rate-limiting expectations.
- Provide an allowlist IP (if you want more control) and confirm if PI I will be excluded during hosted tests.

If you prefer the dedicated path we should start the paperwork and capacity reservation now; Alex can send the capacity/commit options after the kickoff. For VPC we'll need a short security checklist and a network engineer on the kickoff.

I'll drop the runbook in the shared Drive and bring Alex to the kickoff to run the infra checklist.

See you Tuesday — thanks,
Marissa
